saints.name: St. Agatha
saints.title: Virgin and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: A noble maiden of Sicily who suffered a cruel martyrdom for Christ, and whose name stands in the Canon of the Mass…
biography: A maiden of noble family at Catania in Sicily, born about 231, Agatha consecrated her virginity to Christ and, in the persecution of Decius, rejected the advances of Quintianus, the consular of Sicily. Denounced by him as a Christian, she was imprisoned, stretched on the rack, and torn with iron hooks; her breasts were cut off.

In her cell, her acts relate, the Apostle Peter appeared and healed her wounds; when she was sentenced to the fire, an earthquake stayed the sentence, and she died of her torments in prison about the year 251. Her veneration spread at once through East and West, and her name entered the Canon of the Mass among the virgin-martyrs.

In the year after her death the stilling of an eruption of Etna was ascribed to her intercession, whence she is invoked against fire, as against diseases of the breast from the manner of her torture. She is the patroness of Catania, whose great festival in her honour still fills the first days of February.
saints.knownFor: Her steadfast martyrdom in Sicily and her name in the Roman Canon.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 5 February
